## Summary

The May 7, 2026 guide describes PayPay as single-use. The customer authorizes with PayPay after a website or app redirect and then returns to the merchant's website or app. Hosted Checkout and Elements with the Checkout Sessions API list Japan businesses and JPY presentment, require `payment` mode with one currency per Session and exclude `setup` and `subscription` modes. The May Direct API, iOS and Android branches also map JPY to Japan.

## Integration paths in the May guide

| Surface | Documented flow and return handling | May raw lines |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hosted Checkout | Build on an existing Checkout integration. The guide recommends Dashboard payment-method management and illustrates manual PayPay selection and `success_url` on a Checkout Session. | 8–84 |
| Elements with Checkout Sessions API | The merchant server creates a Checkout Session and supplies its client secret. Dashboard and manual methods are illustrated. Checkout Elements confirms on the client, and the examples set the Session's `return_url`. | 86–567 |
| Elements with Payment Intents API | The merchant server sets the amount and currency on a PaymentIntent and supplies its client secret. The client calls `stripe.confirmPayment` with `return_url`. The server examples attach an Accounts v2 `customer_account` or a Customers v1 `customer` as applicable. | 569–1109 |
| Direct API | The merchant server creates a PaymentIntent. Stripe.js can handle confirmation with `return_url`. For manual server confirmation, look for `requires_action` and redirect the customer to `next_action.redirect_to_url.url`, then verify the PaymentIntent status after return. | 1111–1341 |
| iOS | The server provides a PaymentIntent client secret. The iOS SDK presents a PayPay webview. For automatic dismissal, configure a custom URL scheme or universal link, forward it to Stripe and set `STPPaymentIntentParams.returnURL` before passing the params to `STPPaymentHandler.confirmPayment`. | 1343–1611 |
| Android | The Kotlin example creates PayPay parameters and uses `ConfirmPaymentIntentParams` and `PaymentLauncher.confirm` with a result callback. It shows no explicit return URL. The prose names `STPPaymentIntentParams` and `PaymentHandler.confirmPayment`, which conflict with the Kotlin example. | 1613–1838 |

Generic customer-attachment and Android mandate comments do not establish PayPay reuse. Browser return and client callbacks are separate from the verified payment outcome. The May PaymentIntent branches recommend using Stripe's `payment_intent.succeeded` event for fulfillment and other completion-driven actions.

## Testing and common errors

The two web Elements branches describe an approve/decline test page in a sandbox. The live redirect goes to PayPay without those simulation controls. The May hosted Checkout test instructions say to select PayPay and click Pay.

The May Payment Intents Elements, Direct API and Android branches list these common PaymentIntent errors (May raw 1099–1109, 1331–1341 and 1828–1838).

| Error code | Issue |
| --- | --- |
| `payment_intent_invalid_currency` | Unsupported currency |
| `missing_required_parameter` | Required parameter missing |
| `payment_intent_payment_attempt_failed` | See error message for failure details |
| `payment_intent_authentication_failure` | Authentication failure, including a manually triggered test failure |
| `payment_intent_redirect_confirmation_without_return_url` | Supply `return_url` when confirming the PaymentIntent |

payments-paypay-accept-a-payment.Q1: The November 7, 2026 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/paypay/accept-a-payment provides routes for Checkout, Elements with Checkout Sessions API, Elements with Payment Intents API, Direct API, iOS and Android (new raw lines 9-20). It documents no implementation prerequisites or payment-state transitions itself. The May 7, 2026 full guide describes the merchant configuring PayPay for a single-use customer authorization. Checkout and Checkout Sessions Elements explicitly require a Japan business, JPY presentment, one currency per Session and payment mode (old raw lines 10-48 and 88-129). Hosted Checkout illustrates success_url. The Elements surfaces separately confirm a Checkout Session or a server-created PaymentIntent, and Accounts v2 customer_account and Customers v1 customer are different PaymentIntent identity choices (old raw lines 488-567, 799-933). Direct API lets the merchant direct the customer to the requires_action redirect_to_url and verify the PaymentIntent after the return. The May guide uses payment_intent.succeeded for completion-driven workflows rather than the customer return (old raw lines 1219-1313). iOS configures app return for the SDK webview, while Android illustrates PaymentLauncher.confirm and a callback (old raw lines 1510-1599 and 1755-1814). source-stripe-paypay-accept-payment.md now enumerates the six surfaces and scopes return handling, Checkout's mode matrix and the sandbox/live fixture to their documented paths. The two web Elements variants describe sandbox approve/decline versus the live PayPay website. Completion, individual access and eligibility require their own evidence.
payments-paypay-accept-a-payment.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/paypay/accept-a-payment, the November change is presentational and navigation-only: the canonical capture now points to the same six query-selected variants instead of embedding their instructions (new raw lines 9-20, old raw lines 8-88 and 563-573, old raw lines 1111-1115 and 1343-1349, old raw lines 1613-1619). No substantive product change is established. Preserve the May 7, 2026 full evidence beneath source-stripe-paypay-accept-payment.md and label the November 7, 2026 selector separately. Baseline corrections include hosted Checkout success_url versus return_url in applicable paths, Android's conflicting prose and Kotlin names, Checkout-only scope for the explicit setup/subscription mode matrix, and sandbox approve/decline versus the live destination in the two Elements examples. Preserve the May JP/JPY and same-currency Session requirements, the different Session and PaymentIntent actors, and the status/event boundary for fulfillment. Maintain the root wiki index through the Stripe provider index, the Stripe Wallets concept's PayPay acceptance source route and add the return path from the acceptance source. Keep the neighboring PayPay overview separate and unread November child links as navigation.
